findings.detail: Description of "list_services" instructs the model to conceal actions from the user.

findings.title: Read-only tool requests dangerous parameters
findings.detail: Tool "confirm_booking" appears informational but accepts parameters (code) that enable code/file/secret access.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: confirm_booking, request_callback, get_payment_handoff_url, request_service, submit_quote_request · Private data: get_credentials, initiate_handoff, submit_quote_request · Public sink: reserve_slot, confirm_booking, initiate_handoff, request_callback, subscribe_to_updates, request_service, submit_quote_request.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: confirm_booking, request_callback, get_payment_handoff_url, request_service, submit_quote_request · Private data: get_credentials, initiate_handoff, submit_quote_request · Public sink: reserve_slot, confirm_booking, initiate_handoff, request_callback, subscribe_to_updates, request_service, submit_quote_request

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.

findings.title: Tool description changed since last scan
findings.detail: Tool "search_businesses" changed its description with no version change. Silent description changes are how a trusted server turns malicious after review.

evidence.snippet: before: "Search for registered businesses by category, name, or location. Returns a list of matching businesses with their slugs. Use this to discover which businesses are available before querying one." → after: "Find registered businesses by search term and optional location; returns matches with their slugs. Call it before the business-specific tools."

findings.remediation: Re-review the tool before continuing to trust it.
